research.summary: Google's Spam policy FAQ explicitly forbids a developer rating or reviewing their own extension from any account, and extends that to "other developers or users that are affiliated with the publisher"; the Program Policies say manipulating reviews or ratings gets a developer banned. The most likely reasons friends' reviews are invisible, from Google's own docs and Chrome DevRel (Oliver Dunk) statements on the chromium-extensions group: (a) the reviewer must have installed the item from the Chrome Web Store; (b) the new store filters the reviews page to the viewer's current language by default (an "All languages" switch was added 27 Mar 2024); (c) since Jan 2025 the main listing page no longer shows review bodies, only the /reviews page does, and header ratings are recalculated periodically so they lag; (d) reviews can be "held for moderation or deleted" with no developer-visible detail and no published timeframe (DevRel: wait "a couple of days before becoming concerned"); (e) the item must actually be published, and AuthPeek's own site still says the listing is "in review". No Google source was found for a minimum-ratings threshold, age/Workspace restrictions on reviewing, or region-based review partitioning (a third-party scraper says reviews partition by language, not country). Developers see and reply to reviews in the item's Reviews section and the dashboard's Ratings page; incentivized reviews are explicitly prohibited, while plainly asking genuine users for an honest review is not addressed in any policy text found.

findings.claim: A developer may not rate or review their own extension from any account, and reviews from affiliated people (which would include group-publisher members and friends acting on the developer's behalf) are treated the same way.
findings.detail: Google's Spam policy FAQ (section "User ratings, reviews, and installs", last updated 2020-05-01) asks "Can I review or rate my own extension?" and answers: "No. Submitting a rating or review of your own extension, using your own account or other accounts, may be interpreted as an attempt to manipulate the extension's placement in the Chrome Web Store. This also includes ratings and reviews coming from other developers or users that are affiliated with the publisher." The same FAQ defines manipulating placement as "artificially manipulating how the Chrome Web Store orders and displays an extension" and says "Such practices are expressly forbidden." The consequence is in the Program Policies' "Best Practices and Guidelines" item 3: "No cheating. If you attempt to scam the system (for example, by misleading users, circumventing enforcement, copying the work of other developers, or manipulating your extension's reviews or ratings) you will be banned from the Chrome Web Store." The group-publishers doc (last updated 2026-04-15) says nothing about reviews. I found no Google documentation stating whether the store UI technically blocks the publisher account from submitting a rating (the user reports they "can't" do it); that mechanical detail is unconfirmed.

findings.claim: Only users who have installed the item from the Chrome Web Store can rate or review it; Google does not verify reviews but removes ones that violate its terms, and anyone can report a review.
findings.detail: Chrome Web Store Help, "Chrome Web Store curation and reviews": "Users who have installed an item from the Chrome Web Store can provide a rating and a written review. Google doesn't verify the authenticity of reviews and ratings, but reviews that violate our terms of service will be removed. Users may report an abusive review from the review section of the item listing page." The same page says "The number of ratings and the average rating are taken into account when prioritizing items." The "Tips for using the Chrome Web Store" help page repeats: "You can rate or review an app, extension or theme after you have installed it," with steps "Select the item to review" > "Click Reviews" > "Rate the item with 1-5 stars" > "Add your review in the comments box." Developer docs add: "Each user can only rate an extension once, but they can update their rating or review at any time." Implication for the friends' case: a friend who installed via the GitHub zip / unpacked load rather than from the store listing would not meet this condition.

findings.claim: The new Chrome Web Store shows reviews filtered to the viewer's current language by default; an "All languages" option exists on the /reviews page (added March 2024), so reviews written in another language are hidden until the viewer switches it.
findings.detail: In the chromium-extensions thread "PSA: Preview rollout of the new Chrome Web Store", Oliver Dunk (DevRel, Chrome Extensions) wrote on Aug 25, 2023: "At the moment, I believe we only show reviews from your own language," and on Aug 31, 2023: "At the moment, we show reviews filtered based on your current language. If you'd like to see reviews from other languages, you can change your overall language in the store." Developers complained that the new store removed the language/location switcher; a workaround posted Aug 31, 2023 was appending ?hl=<locale> to the /reviews URL (e.g. .../reviews?hl=de). On Mar 27, 2024 Oliver Dunk posted: "I just wanted to share that you can now switch to 'All languages' when looking at reviews." Search-indexed text of a live reviews page (Btools) shows the controls as a rating filter, a "Sort by" menu, and a "Language" selector with "English" and "All languages" — I could not load the store page myself (it redirects to consent.google.com), so the exact labels are medium confidence. A third-party scraper vendor states "The Store returns only reviews written in the requested language" and that the gl (country) parameter has no effect. Practical implication: if the friends wrote in Uzbek/Russian/etc. and the developer views the listing in English, those reviews are hidden until "All languages" is selected.

findings.claim: Since January 2025 the main listing page intentionally no longer displays review bodies (only the /reviews sub-page does); a main page saying "0 reviews"/"No ratings" while reviews exist is a known bug, and the header rating is recalculated periodically so it lags.
findings.detail: Thread "Chrome Web Store Reviews Not Appearing" (chromium-extensions). Oliver Dunk, Jan 17, 2025: "Showing reviews on the main item details pages was something we introduced with the new Chrome Web Store. Based on data we're seeing, the team made a product decision to make that section more concise, and to use the /reviews page to show the actual reviews." Same post: "the behavior you mentioned where the main page explicitly states there are no reviews when reviews are present sounds like a bug. Could you share your extension ID?" A developer (Joel Auge, Jan 15, 2025) described exactly this: "the main extension download page says '0 Reviews', but if you follow the link to read reviews, the reviews are indeed posted." Oliver Dunk, Nov 27, 2025: "The ratings displayed in the header are calculated periodically, and so they can lag behind what you see elsewhere. We've added a little tooltip to make that clearer." Practical check for AuthPeek: open https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/<id>/reviews directly, sort by most recent, and set Language to All languages.

findings.claim: Reviews can be held for moderation or deleted without any developer-visible explanation; Google publishes no timeframe, and DevRel's guidance is to wait a couple of days before worrying. There have also been multi-week store-wide outages where legitimate reviews did not appear.
findings.detail: Oliver Dunk, Nov 22, 2024, answering "how long is typical between email notif and being able to see the review in the store listing?": "I don't think we have a specific time frame, but I would always wait a couple of days before becoming concerned :)". Oliver Dunk, Dec 3, 2025, on a review-notification link leading to a not-found page: "It's likely the message is either being held for moderation or was deleted. Unfortunately, we don't currently have a way to get more details there." Oliver Dunk, Jan 17, 2025: "If you're receiving notifications about reviews which aren't spam, and aren't showing up after a short period of time, please continue to let us know about those. That's definitely unintentional and we can take a look." A developer's unconfirmed hunch (Artem, bardeen.ai, Dec 4, 2024): "some reviews (ones containing links and certain keywords?) get flagged for a manual review and can take a few days to process. Same thing happens to responses to reviews." Documented outage: thread "Chrome Webstore Reviews stopped populating as of Nov 6th for ALL extensions" — reviews with comments stopped appearing from ~Nov 5-6, 2024; Oliver Dunk Nov 13: "this is being actively investigated"; Nov 15: "I believe these should have been restored now"; Nov 18: "it definitely seems like something still isn't right"; Nov 19: "The intent is that all legitimate reviews have been restored for all extensions. If you aren't seeing a review, feel free to send me the email notification you received about it and I can follow up." Developers reported reviews still missing into Dec 2024, Jan 2025 and one Mar 30, 2026 report of two reviews on a featured extension not shown "even after a week" (no reply visible). Note that user review guidelines forbid "emails or links to websites" in reviews, so a friend's review containing a link is a plausible removal cause. The practical escalation path used in these threads is to forward the review-notification email to Chrome Extensions DevRel / post the extension ID in the chromium-extensions group.

findings.claim: Reviews cannot be left on an item that is not yet published; AuthPeek's own public site still says the store listing is "in review", so if friends reviewed before the listing was live their reviews could not have been posted to the public listing.
findings.detail: Derived, not stated in one Google sentence: the curation help page requires that the reviewer "installed an item from the Chrome Web Store", and the publish docs say that after review completes "you will have up to 30 days to publish" and otherwise "the staged submission will revert to a draft" — i.e. an item is not available in the store until published. The AuthPeek GitHub Pages site (fetched 2026-10-23) has no Chrome Web Store link and says the store listing is "in review; the link will be here once it's live." Secondary signal: Windows Report's coverage of a Chromium commit for Chrome's native "Write a review" prompt says eligibility "excludes component, unpacked, unpublished, and removed extensions, along with any extension carrying an active policy violation" (second-hand; the Chromium source itself was not retrieved). I found no Google documentation about what happens to reviews written while an item is pending review or unlisted.

findings.claim: No Google source was found for a minimum number of ratings before an average is displayed, for age-based or Google Workspace restrictions on writing reviews, or for reviews being partitioned by store region.
findings.detail: Minimum threshold: no documentation found; search-indexed listings show a 5.0 average with "6 ratings" and a "No ratings" label at zero, so a small count already displays, but the cutoff (if any) is unconfirmed. A Dec 2023 Indie Hackers post describes a listing showing a star rating but "there are currently no reviews for this item" — consistent with rating-only (no text) reviews or the language filter, but unexplained in the thread. Age/Workspace: the only official page found is the Workspace admin article on turning the Chrome Web Store on or off per organizational unit; a user whose admin has disabled the store cannot install and therefore cannot review (inference). Nothing found on Family Link/under-18 review restrictions. Region: the old help page says store Settings > Language and Location control which items you see "available in your country"; a third-party scraper vendor says the store partitions reviews by language and that the gl (country) parameter has no effect. Treat all three as unconfirmed.

findings.claim: Developers see reviews in the item's Reviews section (where they can post and edit replies but never delete user reviews), get an overview in the developer dashboard's Ratings page under Analytics, and can enable email alerts and a Support hub in Account settings.
findings.detail: "Manage user feedback" (developer.chrome.com, last updated 2021-08-17): "Users can leave comments in the Reviews section of your store item, under the item's overview. You can also post replies here to those reviews." "You can also edit your reply at any time to provide the user with updates." "you cannot remove user comments from your listing, even if you believe they are unfair." "Users are more likely to improve their reviews if you respond and address their concerns promptly." "The Rating tab in the developer dashboard provides an overview of your extension's ratings, including the total number of reviews and ratings over time." Email alerts: Account settings > Notifications > enable "Item review completed" ("To receive email notifications when users post reviews or update existing reviews"). Support hub: "The Chrome Web Store provides a support hub, where users can leave questions, suggestions, and issues they are facing"; it must be enabled under "Item support visibility" in Account settings, or a custom Support URL can be set in the Store Listing tab; "Users won't be notified when you reply to a support issue." Dashboard menu (CWS analytics revamp post): Build = Package, Store listing, Privacy, Pricing & Distribution; Analytics = Installs & Uninstalls, Impressions, Weekly Users, Ratings. On the new store only developer replies are shown and they carry a "Developer" badge (Oliver Dunk, Aug 31, 2023: "we are still showing replies to reviews, but only from the developer"); he also noted (Dec 2023) a sync delay "of up to a few days" for replies/badges. One developer (Dec 20, 2024) reported that a review missing from the listing was also absent from Developer Dashboard > Rating, so the dashboard is not guaranteed to show held reviews.

findings.claim: Policy explicitly bans incentivized or fraudulent reviews/ratings/installs and self/affiliated reviews; it does not contain any text forbidding a plain, non-incentivized request to genuine users for an honest review.
findings.detail: Program Policies, "Spam and Abuse" (last updated 2022-11-01): "Developers must not attempt to manipulate the placement of any extensions in the Chrome Web Store. This includes, but is not limited to, inflating product ratings, reviews, or install counts by illegitimate means, such as fraudulent or incentivized downloads, reviews and ratings." Spam FAQ: "Can I provide incentives for users to download my extension? No. The offer of incentives to download a Chrome Web Store extension is not allowed... The features of your extension should be incentive enough." and the self/affiliated-review answer quoted above. User-side review guidelines (Tips page): "Don't post fake reviews intended to boost or lower ratings"; "Don't include emails or links to websites or other apps in your review"; "Don't pretend to be someone else, or say you're associated with a person or organization you don't know." Neither the FAQ nor the policies address asking users for reviews without an incentive; the developer doc only encourages replying to reviews. Asking friends is the risky case specifically because the FAQ treats "users that are affiliated with the publisher" as placement manipulation.

findings.claim: Other review/rating-related rules a new developer should watch: no testimonials in the description, no metadata misrepresenting store status/performance, severe or repeated violations suspend the developer account and related accounts, and from Aug 2026 the displayed rating weights recent reviews more.
findings.detail: Program Policies (last updated 2025-05-22), Listing Requirements: "We don't allow unattributed or anonymous user testimonials in the product's description." Impersonation & Intellectual Property: prohibits "Any metadata that misrepresents the extension's or developer's current status or performance on the Chrome Web Store" (e.g. claiming a rating or 'featured' status you do not have). Repeat Abuse: "Serious or repeated violations of the Chrome Web Store Distribution Agreement or these Program Policies will result in the suspension of your developer account, and possibly related developer accounts. Additionally, you may be banned from using the Chrome Web Store. In extreme cases, this may also result in the suspension of related Google services associated with your Google account." Enforcement Circumvention: "Any attempt to circumvent intended limitations or enforcement actions will result in the immediate termination of your developer account, and possibly related developer accounts." Appeals: "Developers are permitted to appeal a violation decision once." Chrome Web Store blog, Aug 20, 2026 (Kevin Bay): "Going forward, the extension rating will focus on more recent reviews to better reflect current user sentiments" (aligned with Google Play); the same post sunsets the "Featured" badge program and sets a default publication limit of "two extension slots" per publisher, with increases requestable from the dashboard. Google's review-process documentation (via search summary, not fetched directly) says some signals cause closer review, "including new developers".

research.summary: Google documents only a handful of ranking inputs for Chrome Web Store search: item name, description relevancy, popularity (installs vs uninstalls over time), user experience, and the number and average of ratings — with the rating now weighted toward recent reviews (Aug 20, 2026). Listing metadata (title ≤75 chars, summary ≤132 chars, description, category, language, images) is explicitly described as what search ranks on, and keyword spam (>5 repeats, lists of brands/sites/regions) can get an item suspended. The Featured badge is being sunset and self-nominations closed on Aug 20, 2026, so it is no longer a target; the Established Publisher badge is automatic once the publisher is "verified" — which Google's own link defines as choosing an Official URL from sites verified in Google Search Console, and having a few months of clean policy history. Localized listings are per-locale description/screenshots/video driven by _locales (AuthPeek currently has none), and the Language field exists "to allow users to search for extensions in their own language", but Google states no ranking boost. On reviews: only users who installed the item can review; rating or reviewing your own extension, or reviews from "users affiliated with the publisher", may be treated as placement manipulation; reviews flagged as spam never count toward the published total; Google has had store-wide review-display outages (Nov 2024) and a pattern of emailed-but-invisible reviews reported Dec 2024 with no public staff explanation. Competitor listings in this niche use "Brand - 2FA/TOTP/OTP keyword phrase" titles and front-load "2FA codes in your browser", "no phone needed", "import from Google Authenticator", "autofill" in the 132-char summary; the dominant competitor ("Authenticator", ~10M users) sits in Privacy & Security, which is also where "Productivity" (AuthPeek's chosen category, retired in mid-2023) maps. No primary-source search-volume data for authenticator keywords was found.

findings.claim: Google's official ranking inputs for store search and recommendations: item name, description relevancy, popularity, user experience, number of ratings and average rating.
findings.detail: Chrome Web Store Help, 'Chrome Web Store Curation and Reviews', section 'Organizing and ranking Chrome Web Store items': "Relevancy: Search ranking and recommendations are ordered based on the item name, description relevancy, popularity, and user experience." and "User popularity: The number of ratings and the average rating are taken into account when prioritizing items." Also: "Items featured on the Chrome Web Store are manually selected based on specific eligibility criteria." The developer doc 'Discovery on the Chrome Web Store' adds that search "returns a list of items that are ranked based on a number of criteria, including metadata from your item's listing page" and that the badge-ranking heuristic "takes into account ratings from users and usage statistics, such as downloads versus uninstalls over time", plus visual design, a clear purpose meeting a real need, intuitive setup/onboarding, and ease of use. The same page says badge holders "may receive higher rankings in search and filtering". Note: the discovery page shows "Last updated 2022-03-21 UTC" and predates the 2026 badge changes. Google does not publish weights; install count is only referenced as 'popularity' / 'downloads versus uninstalls'.

findings.claim: Listing fields and limits: title ≤75 characters (manifest name), summary ≤132 characters plain text (manifest description, shown in search results), plus description, category, language, icon 128x128, 1–5 screenshots 1280x800 (or 640x400), small promo tile 440x280 (shown in search results), marquee 1400x560, optional YouTube video, official/homepage/support URLs.
findings.detail: Manifest 'name': "a short, plain text string (maximum of 75 characters) that identifies the extension", displayed in the install dialog, chrome://extensions and the Chrome Web Store. Manifest 'description': "A plain text string (no HTML or other formatting; no more than 132 characters)", which the 'Creating a great listing page' doc says "appears on the homepage, category pages, and in search results" (the store 'summary'). The dashboard doc: store icon 128x128 required; "At least one 1280x800 px screenshot, up to 5 total"; small promo tile 440x280 PNG/JPEG; marquee 1400x560 PNG/JPEG; image quality "can affect your item's prominence on the Chrome Web Store"; Language field: "Your item's language to allow users to search for extensions in their own language"; the mature-content toggle hides the item from search for logged-out users. Best-listing doc: small promo tile "Appears on the homepage, category pages, and in search results"; marquee used only if chosen for the homepage carousel; website and support URLs "help build trust". AuthPeek's current values (docs/store-listing.md and extension/manifest.json): name 'AuthPeek – Authenticator & Code Autofill' = 42 chars; summary = 113 chars; both within limits. Note: manifest metadata cannot be edited in the dashboard after upload — a title/summary change requires a new version upload ('Prepare your extension').

findings.claim: Google's listing best practices: descriptive, un-stuffed title; summary without superlatives or competitor references; description = overview paragraph + short feature list with keywords for the most important features; promo images must not claim 'Editor's Choice'/'Number One'.
findings.detail: 'Creating a great listing page': Title should be "clear and descriptive, concise, and unique"; "Don't stuff the title with keywords." Summary: "Avoid generic phrases, superlatives such as 'greatest' and 'fastest,' and references to competing extensions." Description: "Recommended format: an overview paragraph followed by a short list of main features"; "Focus on keywords that represent the most important features. Don't add unnecessary keywords, since keyword spam can get an item suspended." Screenshots: show actual UX of the latest version, "square corners and no padding (full bleed)", limit text, locale-specific screenshots supported. Promo images: "Don't make claims that misrepresent your item's status, such as 'Editor's Choice' or 'Number One'"; use saturated colors, fill the region, work at half size. The 'Best practices' doc: "The purpose of an extension's Chrome Web Store store listing is to set the user's expectations"; follow the Branding guidelines for name/description/logo; "Images should not be blurry or too busy."

findings.claim: What gets a listing rejected, demoted or suspended: blank description or missing icon/screenshots (automatic rejection); inaccurate/incomplete metadata; keyword spam (lists of sites/brands/keywords, lists of regions, >5 repeats of a keyword); unattributed testimonials; privacy-field contradictions; incentivized or self/affiliate reviews; duplicate per-language extensions.
findings.detail: Listing Requirements policy: "If your product has a blank description field or is missing an icon or screenshots, it will be rejected." Metadata must not be "misleading, inaccurate, incomplete, improperly formatted, non-descriptive" — covering description, category, developer name, title, icon, screenshots, promo images. "Keyword Spam is the practice of including irrelevant or excessive keywords in an extensions description in an attempt to manipulate its ranking"; examples: "Lists of sites/brands/keywords without substantial added value", "Lists of regional locations", "Unnatural repetition of the same keyword more than 5 times". "We don't allow unattributed or anonymous user testimonials in the product's description." Privacy fields contradicting the privacy policy or actual behavior → removal. Spam Policy FAQ: "it's best to keep instances of a specific keyword to under 5" (allowed if "appropriate and relevant"; the puzzle example says even the primary-purpose word should stay under 5 "unless its use is critical"); no more than five brands/websites listed; repeating the short description inside the description "would not be considered a violation"; extensions that "differ only in localization" are a repetitive-content violation — ship all languages in one extension. Spam and Abuse policy: no inflating "ratings, reviews, or install counts by illegitimate means" including "fraudulent or incentivized downloads, reviews and ratings". Applied to AuthPeek's current description (docs/store-listing.md): 'code' appears 10 times (incl. 'codes' 6), 'fill' 4, 'authenticator' 3, 'Google Authenticator' 2, 'QR' 3, 'encrypted' 3 — 'code(s)' exceeds the under-5 guideline, though arguably 'critical' to an authenticator's purpose.

findings.claim: The Featured badge is being discontinued: self-nominations closed on August 20, 2026 and the program is being sunset 'later this year'; Google tells developers to focus on the refreshed rating instead.
findings.detail: Chrome for Developers blog, 'Chrome Web Store updates: Faster reviews, new publication limits, badge updates, and more' by Kevin Bay, Published: August 20, 2026: "we're sunsetting the 'Featured' badge program later this year, encouraging developers to focus on our refreshed rating system as the strongest signal of an extension's quality." "Self-nominations will close today and all currently pending self-nominations will be closed." Reason given: baseline review investments "made the badge a less meaningful signal". Historical criteria (now moot) from the 2022 Google blog and the discovery doc: manual review for adherence to best practices (UX, current APIs, privacy) and a clear listing with quality images and detailed description; nominee had to be a public extension with English support, no active violations, core features usable without extra credentials or payment; nominations went through the One Stop Support form. In the chromium-extensions thread on the announcement, developer Alesandro Ortiz asked what now determines search-bar suggestions since the badge "was historically the main criterion" — no Google answer visible. The 'Featured Products' policy still lists categories Google won't feature (VPNs, antivirus, crypto, downloaders, gambling, non-production builds, developers with "questionable reputations"); authenticators are not on that list.

findings.claim: The store rating now weights recent reviews; each publisher account defaults to two extension slots (Aug 20, 2026).
findings.detail: Same Aug 20, 2026 post: "Going forward, the extension rating will focus on more recent reviews to better reflect current user sentiments and to be aligned with other marketplaces, such as Google Play." Publication limits: "each publisher account has an updated extension limit, with a default of two extension slots"; existing items stay published; increases can be requested in the dashboard "and will receive an immediate response in most cases". Oliver Dunk (Chrome Extensions DevRel) clarified in the thread that the limit "applies to all public items, including unlisted items" and "does not apply to private items including published to trusted testers or domain." Implication: a steady flow of fresh ratings matters more than a historical average, and there is no room for separate variant listings (e.g. a 'lite' or per-language copy).

findings.claim: The Established Publisher badge is granted automatically to publishers whose identity is verified (Google's link defines this as the Official URL / Search Console verified-publisher flow) and who have months of clean policy history; ~75% of extensions have it; it cannot be bought.
findings.detail: Discovery doc: granted when "The publisher's identity has been verified" and "The publisher has a consistent positive track record with Google services and complies with the Developer Program Policy"; "New developers need at least a few months of compliance"; "this badge covers nearly 75 percent of extensions in the store"; "Developers cannot pay for either badge." In both the discovery doc and the 2022 Google blog, the word "verified" hyperlinks to https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/cws-dashboard-listing#displaying-your-verified-publisher-status — i.e. identity verification = displaying verified publisher status via an Official URL. The 2022 blog describes the badge as "a small check mark next to the developer's website name". Whether contact-email verification alone suffices is not stated (low confidence on that sub-point).

findings.claim: How to link the GitHub Pages site as the item's website: verify it in Google Search Console under the same Google account, then pick it in the Store listing tab's 'Official URL' pull-down; verified publishers get a linked URL under the listing title instead of 'Offered by: <name>'.
findings.detail: Dashboard listing doc, 'Display your verified publisher status': "The Chrome Web Store highlights verified publishers by placing a linked, official URL under the listing title"; "If you are not a verified publisher, your publisher name will be displayed under the 'Offered by:' in the Details section"; "The pull-down for this field contains only those sites that have been verified as belonging to you." "To add a verified site that you own, click on Add a new site" — "This opens the Google Search Console, where you can add and verify a site." Separate 'Homepage URL' (appears under Details) and 'Support URL' fields also exist. Search Console constraints for https://lazizjanasatov.github.io/Authpeek/: a Domain property needs a DNS record ("the only way to verify a Domain property") — not possible on github.io; a URL-prefix property can be verified by HTML tag "into the <head> section in the HTML of your site's non-logged-in home page" or by HTML file "available at the address specified in the verification details page"; HTML tag/file/Analytics/Tag Manager "Can be used for URL-prefix properties, but not Domain properties"; path-based child properties like "https://example.com/some/path" are auto-verified from a verified parent. For AuthPeek the practical route is a URL-prefix property for https://lazizjanasatov.github.io/Authpeek/ with the meta tag in docs/index.html. Unconfirmed (low confidence): whether the CWS Official URL pull-down accepts a path-level URL-prefix property vs host-level only, and the third-party claim (roboin.io) that the publishing account needs Owner-level Search Console access and that approval took a day.

findings.claim: Publisher pages (Nov 5, 2025) are reachable from the Official URL but are initially only for organizations verified as traders; all developers must self-declare trader/non-trader status under the EU DSA.
findings.detail: Blog 'Publisher pages: New to the Chrome Web Store' (Nov 5, 2025): users reach the page "by clicking an eligible publisher's official URL at the top of an item page"; initially for "any publisher owned by an organization and verified as a trader"; the spotlight item defaults to "the highest-ranking item by an internal Chrome Web Store score". Trader docs: "All developers on the Chrome Web Store are required to declare if they are a Trader or Non-Trader"; for non-traders the consumer is told consumer-protection rights do not apply. A solo individual developer is therefore not currently eligible for a publisher page.

findings.claim: Localized listings: name/summary localize through _locales/<code>/messages.json with default_locale; description, screenshots and video can be localized per locale in the dashboard; promo tiles cannot; Google says the Language field lets users search 'in their own language' but states no ranking boost for localized listings.
findings.detail: Dashboard listing doc, 'Localize your listing': "If you have localized your extension, you will be able to provide a description, screenshots, and promotional video in the locales your extension supports." "The small tile and Marquee promo tile cannot be localized." "Each locale corresponds to one of the _locales/LOCALE_CODE directories included in the extension." Locales are chosen from the language dropdown at the top of the Store listing tab. Display order: localized video, localized screenshots, global video, global screenshots. A metadata-inconsistency warning across locales "doesn't block submission". By default the item is listed in all regions; the Distribution tab narrows regions. i18n API doc: with a /_locales directory "the manifest must define 'default_locale'"; name/description use __MSG_name__ placeholders; lookup falls back user locale → language → default locale; "You can localize your extension to any locale that is supported by the Chrome Web Store" (e.g. de_CH → de). Language field purpose: "to allow users to search for extensions in their own language". No Google page found that promises higher visibility in a locale for having a translated listing — only that the localized text is what users in that locale see and search against (inference). The old /docs/webstore/i18n listing page returns 404 and could not be retrieved via archive. Repo check: AuthPeek has no _locales directory (manifest name/description are hard-coded English), so no localized listing is possible until that is added.

findings.claim: Category: 'Productivity' (used in AuthPeek's store-listing.md) was retired in mid-2023; its replacements include 'Privacy & Security' and 'Tools', and the leading authenticator extensions sit in 'Privacy & Security'.
findings.detail: 'Best practices' doc: mid-2023 category change replaced Fun, Photos, Productivity and Social & Communications; Productivity maps to Education, Functionality & UI, Household, Privacy & Security, Tools, Workflow & Planning. Current 18 categories include Privacy & Security and Tools. Discovery doc: categories organize items "based on their main function", set in Product Details. Per extscope.org mirrors of the store: 'Authenticator' (authenticator.cc), '2FAS Auth' and 'Bitwarden Password Manager' are in Privacy & Security; smaller TOTP extensions use Tools. docs/store-listing.md and docs/deploy-checklist.md both still say 'Productivity'.

findings.claim: Using 'Google Authenticator' or 'Chrome' in the title/description: Google trademarks may not be used as the extension name or logo; compatibility phrasing ('for', 'for use with', 'compatible with') with ™ and an attribution line is allowed; metadata must not imply Google endorsement.
findings.detail: Branding guidelines: "Don't use any Google trademarks or any confusingly similar marks as the name of your extension or company" (written permission required); same for logos. Compatibility: reference the Google product using "for", "for use with" or "compatible with", include ™ (example "for Google Chrome™"), and "Give proper attribution for the use of any Google trademarks in your extension title or in your description" — sample: "Google Maps is a trademark of Google LLC. Use of this trademark is subject to Google Permissions." Impersonation policy: "don't represent that your product is authorized by, endorsed by, or produced by another company"; metadata misrepresenting status is not allowed; IP concerns can affect visibility. Observed practice: a chromewebstore-restricted search for 'Google Authenticator' returns only third-party extensions (no official Google extension exists), and competitors write 'Quick import from Google Authenticator' / 'Alternative to Google Authenticator' in summaries; one Turkish listing adds the trademark notice. AuthPeek's description mentions 'Google Authenticator' twice without ™ or an attribution line.

findings.claim: Reviews/ratings rules relevant to the developer's problem: only users who installed the item can review; Google removes TOS-violating reviews and does not count spam-flagged ones; rating your own extension (any account) or reviews from people 'affiliated with the publisher' may be treated as placement manipulation; incentivized reviews are prohibited; developers cannot delete reviews.
findings.detail: Help Center: "Users who have installed an item from the Chrome Web Store can provide a rating and a written review." "Google doesn't verify the authenticity of reviews and ratings, but reviews that violate our terms of service will be removed." Spam FAQ: "Submitting a rating or review of your own extension" may be treated as an attempt to manipulate placement, whether from your own account or others, and "also includes ratings and reviews coming from other developers or users that are affiliated with the publisher"; incentives to install are not allowed. Spam & Abuse policy forbids inflating ratings/reviews/installs via "fraudulent or incentivized downloads, reviews and ratings". 'Manage user feedback' doc: "Each user can only rate an extension once, but they can update their rating or review at any time"; "you cannot remove user comments from your listing"; developers can reply (users are not notified); enable the 'Item review completed' notification in Account settings; append /reviews to the item URL for the review page; the dashboard Rating tab shows totals over time. Simeon Vincent (Chrome Extensions DevRel, Jul 1, 2021): "If they were flagged as spam, the total number of published reviews wouldn't change." None of these pages state a minimum number of reviews before reviews display (low confidence that no such threshold exists).

findings.claim: Reviews not appearing is a recurring, Google-acknowledged store-side problem: a store-wide outage Nov 6–15, 2024 was confirmed and 'restored' by Chrome DevRel; in Dec 2024 many developers reported review-notification emails for reviews that never showed on the listing, with no public staff explanation.
findings.detail: Thread 'Chrome Webstore Reviews stopped populating as of Nov 6th for ALL extensions': Oliver Dunk (DevRel, Chrome Extensions) Nov 13, 2024: "We're seeing the same and this is being actively investigated." Nov 15, 2024: "I believe these should have been restored now and new reviews should be appearing." Thread 'Chrome Web Store Reviews Not Appearing' (Dec 4–21, 2024): multiple developers report reviews emailed via notifications but absent from the listing and even from the dashboard Rating page; a developer (not staff) speculated reviews with links/keywords "get flagged for a manual review and can take a few days to process". Search-engine snippets of these groups.google.com threads also attribute to Google staff that a missing review is "either being held for moderation or was deleted", that the full review list "moved ... to the /reviews page", and that header ratings "are calculated periodically, and so they can lag" — I could not retrieve those exact posts (Google Groups pages load lazily), so treat those three quotes as low confidence. Practical checks implied by the threads: open <item URL>/reviews, check the dashboard Rating tab, allow several days, confirm the reviewer installed from the store and is signed in.

findings.claim: How competitors title and summarize authenticator listings (third-party mirrors of the store, since store pages redirect to a consent wall): titles are 'Brand[ - 2FA/TOTP/OTP keyword phrase]'; summaries front-load 'codes in your browser', 'no phone needed', 'import from Google Authenticator', 'autofill'.
findings.detail: Authenticator (authenticator.cc): title "Authenticator"; summary "Authenticator generates two-factor authentication codes in your browser."; ~10M users, 3.6★ from 2,486 ratings; Privacy & Security. 2FAS: title "2FAS Auth - Two Factor Authentication"; summary "2FAS Browser Extension is simple, private, and secure: 1 click, 1 tap, and your token is automatically entered!"; ~90K users (extscope) / 60K+ (chromeboard), 3.5★ (130); Privacy & Security. "2FA Authenticator" (authenticator.sh): summary "Fast, offline 2FA codes in your browser — TOTP two-factor authentication. Quick import from Google Authenticator."; 200K users, 4.6★ (269); Tools (one review alleges malware — unverified). "2FA Authenticator" (TypingDNA): "Generates two-factor codes in your browser. Alternative to Google Authenticator. No phone needed."; 100K, 3.4★ (54). "TOTP Authenticator - 2FA OTP Code Generator": "Secure and fast TOTP authenticator for 2FA login. Generate OTP codes offline and manage multiple accounts easily."; 2K, 5.0★ (9). "Authenticator - 2FA & TOTP Code Generator": "2FA & TOTP authenticator code generator with QR scanning, smart 1-click autofill, encrypted backups and optional Chrome Sync". Other indexed titles for the 'authenticator'/'2FA autofill' queries: "2FA Live — Authenticator & OTP Code Generator", "Auto 2FA OTP", "2FA Autofill", "Authenticator Pro", "Authenticator for PC", "2! Authenticator", "Authenticator Extension", "2FA Authenticator Guard". Google indexes listing pages as '<Title> - Chrome Web Store', so the 75-char title also drives the Google Search result title. Not in the store: Bitwarden's extension is "Bitwarden Password Manager" (8M users) whose summary does not mention TOTP (TOTP is a premium feature); 'Bitwarden Authenticator' is a mobile app with no Chrome listing found; Microsoft Autofill was retired Dec 14, 2024 and no Microsoft Authenticator extension was found; Ente Auth has no official extension (only an unofficial GitHub project neekrom/ente-auth-ext). User/rating figures come from extscope.org/chromeboard.com mirrors, not the store itself.

findings.claim: No primary-source data on which search terms users type in the Chrome Web Store ('authenticator', '2FA', 'TOTP', 'autofill 2FA codes', 'Google Authenticator for Chrome') was found; Google publishes no store keyword volumes.
findings.detail: Searches for keyword volume returned only third-party SEO blogs with no figures. The only observable proxy is which terms competitors put in titles/summaries (see competitor finding): 'Authenticator', '2FA', 'TOTP', 'OTP', 'two-factor', 'code generator', 'autofill', 'Google Authenticator' (as import/alternative phrasing). Third-party advice that titles should stay under ~36 characters to avoid truncation in result cards is unverified. Google Keyword Planner / Trends would be needed for actual volumes.

findings.claim: Operational facts for a new listing: indexing takes a few hours; check region selection on the Distribution tab; collections are curated and cannot be solicited; homepage featuring is editorial and cannot be paid for.
findings.detail: Discovery doc: "A newly published extension may take a few hours to be indexed. Developers should also check the regions selected on the Distribution tab." Collections "are not intended to be comprehensive"; "Solicitations to be placed in a collection are not accepted." Homepage features are curated "based on a variety of factors including performance, design, usefulness, relevancy and breadth of appeal"; "Developers cannot pay to be featured on the home page."

research.summary: GEO for AuthPeek, in impact order: (1) get indexed and verified in Search Console: Google says there is nothing extra to do for AI Overviews/AI Mode beyond being indexed and snippet-eligible, and explicitly says no special schema or 'AI text files' (llms.txt) are needed; (2) the Chrome Web Store listing is the asset that actually ranks and gets cited: in live tests today it held positions 1 and 5 on Google and 3 of Perplexity's 10 citations for 'best authenticator extension for Chrome', so its 132-char summary and description are the highest-leverage copy; (3) Perplexity's other citations were competitor-written comparison posts, a listicle, a GitHub repo and a directory, so a neutral comparison page plus mentions in Reddit/HN threads that already rank matter more than on-page tricks (Ahrefs: brand mentions correlate 0.664 with AI Overview visibility vs 0.218 for backlinks; C-SEO Bench finds most on-page GEO methods ineffective); (4) the GitHub Pages site currently lacks canonical, Open Graph, JSON-LD, FAQ, dates, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and the Web Store link, all cheap to add; (5) skip llms.txt and FAQPage markup, never buy or incentivize reviews. No AI Overview rendered for either target query in a signed-out US/English test, so classic organic results are what users and engines currently see. Side finding on the user's review complaint: the new Web Store only shows reviews on the /reviews sub-page, holds some for moderation, and header ratings lag (Chrome DevRel statements).

findings.claim: Google's official position: nothing extra is required for AI Overviews/AI Mode; the only gate is being indexed and snippet-eligible, and Google explicitly says no special schema or 'AI text files' are needed.
findings.detail: Google Search Central 'AI features and your website': "There are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, nor other special optimizations necessary." / "There's also no special schema.org structured data that you need to add." / "You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, or markup to appear in these features." A page must be "indexed and eligible to be shown in Google Search with a snippet"; Googlebot robots.txt is the control (Google-Extended only limits training/grounding in other Google systems); both features use 'query fan-out' (multiple related sub-searches), which is why pages answering narrow sub-questions get pulled in. John Mueller's post of May 21 2025 adds: "Focus on making unique, non-commodity content", "make sure that all the content in your markup is also visible on your web page", "support your textual content with high-quality images and videos", and "More restrictive permissions will limit how your content is featured in our AI experiences." ACTIONS (highest impact, do first): verify https://lazizjanasatov.github.io/Authpeek/ in Search Console and request indexing of / and /privacy.html; never add nosnippet/max-snippet/noindex; give each likely fan-out sub-question (does it sync, is it open source, does it autofill, where are secrets stored) its own H2 with a 1-2 sentence direct answer.

findings.claim: The Chrome Web Store listing page, not the GitHub Pages site, is the asset that ranks and gets cited for the target query today; its summary/description copy is the highest-leverage text.
findings.detail: Live Google search 2026-10-23 (hl=en, gl=us, signed out) for 'best authenticator extension for Chrome': #1 chromewebstore.google.com (Authenticator, 2.5K ratings), #2 authenticator.cc, #3 Reddit r/Bitwarden, then Google Play, #5 chromewebstore.google.com (2FA Authenticator), Softonic, LastPass, YouTube, Proton. For 'how to autofill 2FA codes in Chrome' a Web Store listing (Quickfill – Gmail OTP & 2FA Code Autofill) ranked on page 1 with its listing summary as the snippet. Live Perplexity run same day: 3 of the 10 cited sources were chromewebstore.google.com detail pages. Google's listing guidance: summary "(132 characters or less)"; description "concise, informative, and accurate" with an overview paragraph then a feature list; do not "Add unnecessary keywords to your description in an attempt to improve search results" and "Repetitive or irrelevant use of keywords" can lead to suspension; "at least one—and preferably the maximum allowed five—screenshots" at 1280x800 or 640x400; fill website and support URLs. Discovery doc: store search is "ranked based on a number of criteria, including metadata from your item's listing page"; ranking heuristic "takes into account ratings from users" and "downloads vs. uninstalls over time"; "Promote your listing independently so that it starts to rise in the rankings." Aug 20 2026 CWS update: the Featured badge program is being sunset and the rating will "focus on more recent reviews". ACTIONS: write the 132-char summary as the literal answer to the query (authenticator, 2FA/2-step codes, autofill on login pages, Chrome, encrypted sync, open source, each once); make the description's first paragraph a quotable neutral definition; add site, GitHub and support URLs; 5 current screenshots; once live, put the Web Store URL on the site (currently reads 'in review; the link will be here once it's live') and in README.

findings.claim: Perplexity, for the exact target query, cited competitor-written comparison posts and listicles, a GitHub repo and an extension directory alongside Web Store pages; AuthPeek needs a neutral comparison page and presence in those third-party pages.
findings.detail: Perplexity (signed out, 2026-10-23) answer to 'best authenticator extension for Chrome' recommended Authenticator (authenticator.cc), Bitwarden/1Password and 2FA Authenticator, drew its own comparison table, and cited exactly these 10 URLs: chromewebstore.google.com/detail/authenticator-extension/odfkmgboddhcgopllebhkbjhokpojigd, chromewebstore.google.com/detail/authenticator/bhghoamapcdpbohphigoooaddinpkbai, chromewebstore.google.com/detail/authenticator-app/ioimeaeldphbhdlokejbgcakkihmnpbl, authenticator.sh/blog/best-authenticator-extensions-for-chrome (a competitor's self-published listicle), otpsync.com/blog/otpsync-vs-authenticator-extension (a competitor's 'X vs Y' page), authenticator-2fa.com/authenticator-app-for-chrome/, github.com/authenticator-sh/2fa, claudecodeguides.com/best-authenticator-chrome-extension/, singletabbrowser.com/extension/authenticator (directory), en.softonic.com/downloads/google-authenticator-extension/6. Perplexity's help page only says it gathers from "authoritative sources like articles, websites, and journals" and gives no ranking factors. Vendor data points the same way: HubSpot State of AEO 2026 (Dec 2025–Mar 2026) reports comparison content cited in 95% of tested ChatGPT cases; Wix AI Search Lab (1M+ citations) reports listicles at 21.9% of all citations and 40.86% of commercial-intent citations. The second query could not be tested on Perplexity (anonymous limit redirected to a sign-in wall; I did not sign in). ACTIONS: (a) publish a factual 'AuthPeek vs Google Authenticator vs Authenticator (authenticator.cc) vs Bitwarden' table on the site and a short version in README; (b) publish your own fair 'authenticator extensions for Chrome compared' post that names competitors (the authenticator.sh self-published one was cited); (c) request truthful inclusion in the existing listicles/directories that were cited (authenticator.sh blog, claudecodeguides.com, singletabbrowser.com).

findings.claim: Off-site brand mentions correlate with AI visibility far more than backlinks, and Reddit/Hacker News threads already rank on page 1 for both target queries; answering them (with disclosure) is the cheapest high-impact off-site move.
findings.detail: Ahrefs, May 26 2025, ~75K brands, Spearman correlations with AI Overview brand visibility: branded web mentions 0.664, branded anchors 0.527, branded search volume 0.392, Domain Rating 0.326, referring domains 0.295, backlinks 0.218; Ahrefs: "correlation ≠ causation". Most-cited domains: Ahrefs June 2025 (76.7M AI Overviews, 957K ChatGPT, 953.5K Perplexity prompts): Wikipedia 16.3% ChatGPT / 12.5% Perplexity / 8.4% AIO; YouTube 16.1% Perplexity; Reddit 7.4% AIO. Profound (680M citations, Aug 2024–Jun 2025): Reddit 6.6% of Perplexity, 2.2% of AIO, 1.8% of ChatGPT; G2, TechRadar, PCMag in ChatGPT/Perplexity top 10. Semrush (Jul 14–Oct 12 2025, 230K prompts): Reddit and Wikipedia remain ChatGPT's top two even after a mid-Sept 2025 drop (Reddit ~60%→~10% of responses). github.com, chromewebstore.google.com, producthunt.com, alternativeto.net and news.ycombinator.com appear in none of these top-10 lists. Live Google: r/Bitwarden 'Best 2FA extensions for Google Chrome?' ranked #3 for the target query (plus 'is there an official authenticator extension…', Mar 2026); r/MacOS thread ranked #1 and a Hacker News Show HN (Faktor, Jul 3 2024) ranked on page 1 for the autofill query. ACTIONS: reply in those exact Reddit threads as the developer, factual and disclosed; post a Show HN; ask bloggers/reviewers for mentions (brand name in text), not links.

findings.claim: Classic organic ranking still feeds Google AI Overviews (though less than in 2025), and no AI Overview rendered for either target query in a live signed-out test, so the normal SERP is what users and engines see today.
findings.detail: Ahrefs, Mar 2 2026 (863K keyword SERPs, 4M AI Overview URLs): "37.9% of URLs cited in AI Overviews also appeared within the first 10 blocks"; 31.2% from positions 11–100; 31.0% beyond the top 100 (vs ~76% from the top 10 in July 2025; parsing methodology changed between studies). Google: AI Overviews appear only when its systems determine they add value, so they often do not trigger. Live Google 2026-10-23 (hl=en, gl=us, signed out): neither 'best authenticator extension for Chrome' nor 'how to autofill 2FA codes in Chrome' showed an AI Overview; results were Web Store listings, Reddit, YouTube, Google Help, Softonic, Hacker News, Stack Exchange, Bitwarden forums. ACTION: target the fan-out long tail with dedicated H2s on the one page ('authenticator extension that autofills codes', 'sync authenticator codes between Chrome browsers', 'open source authenticator for Chrome'); the AI Overview test should be repeated signed-in and from other locations before concluding AIO is absent for these queries.

findings.claim: Controlled research (KDD 2024 GEO paper): adding quotations, concrete statistics, cited sources and fluent authoritative prose raised visibility in generative answers by ~28–43%; keyword stuffing reduced it.
findings.detail: Aggarwal et al., 'GEO: Generative Engine Optimization', accepted to KDD 2024, GEO-bench, Table 1 (GPT-3.5 engine): baseline Position-Adjusted Word Count 19.5 → Quotation Addition 27.8 (~+41–43%), Statistics Addition 25.9 (+33%), Fluency Optimization 25.1 (+29%), Cite Sources 24.9 (+28%), Technical Terms 23.1 (+19%), Authoritative 21.8 (+12% PAWC, +19% Subjective Impression), Easy-to-Understand 22.2, Unique Words 20.7, Keyword Stuffing 17.8 (−9%). Abstract: "GEO can boost visibility by up to 40%" and "the efficacy of these strategies varies across domains". ACTIONS for the site, README and Web Store description: state verifiable, numeric facts (version 1.1.3, release date, which encryption primitives and key-derivation are used, exactly which Chrome permissions are requested, that codes are RFC 6238 TOTP, number of automated tests, package size, number of login pages tested); cite the standards/docs you rely on (RFC 6238, chrome.storage.sync docs); write short declarative sentences in a neutral third-person register; do not repeat 'authenticator Chrome extension' as filler.

findings.claim: Counter-evidence (NeurIPS 2025 C-SEO Bench): most on-page 'conversational SEO' methods are ineffective or harmful; being in the retrieved/ranked set matters far more, so on-page GEO polish is hygiene, not the lever.
findings.detail: Puerto et al., 'C-SEO Bench: Does Conversational SEO Work?' (arXiv 2506.11097, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks): "most current C-SEO methods are not only largely ineffective" and often hurt ranking; "traditional SEO strategies, those aiming to improve the ranking of the source in the LLM context" are "significantly more effective"; as more actors adopt them "the overall gains decrease, depicting a congested and zero-sum nature of the problem." ACTION: order of effort should be indexing + Web Store listing + third-party mentions first, then the page-level items below.

findings.claim: Site audit: https://lazizjanasatov.github.io/Authpeek/ has a title and meta description but is missing every other requested on-page element (canonical, Open Graph/Twitter, JSON-LD, FAQ, dates, comparison table, Web Store link, robots.txt, sitemap.xml).
findings.detail: Fetched the live page and read C:\Users\DNS\Desktop\otp\docs\index.html. Present: <title>AuthPeek – 2-step verification codes that fill themselves in</title>; <meta name="description" content="AuthPeek is an authenticator for Chrome: the same 6-digit codes as Google Authenticator, filled into login pages for you. Encrypted with your password, synced with your Google account, no servers.">; H1 '2-step verification codes in Chrome that fill themselves in.'; H2s Why / What it does / Install / How it keeps your codes safe; links to GitHub repo, privacy.html, issues, Buy me a coffee. Missing: <link rel="canonical">, og:*/twitter:* tags, any application/ld+json, FAQ section, visible publish or 'last updated' date, comparison table, Chrome Web Store link (page says 'in review; the link will be here once it's live'), /robots.txt (HTTP 404), /sitemap.xml (HTTP 404), llms.txt. The manifest name is 'AuthPeek – Authenticator & Code Autofill' while the site title contains neither 'authenticator' nor 'autofill'. docs/ is plain HTML (no Jekyll front matter). ACTIONS in order: add the Web Store link when live; canonical; OG/Twitter; dated 'Last updated' line; visible FAQ; comparison table; robots.txt + sitemap.xml; SoftwareApplication JSON-LD.

findings.claim: Title and meta description should carry the words people actually search ('authenticator', 'Chrome extension', '2FA/2-step codes', 'autofill') once each, concisely, following Google's own title/snippet rules.
findings.detail: Google title-link doc: "Write descriptive and concise text for your <title> elements"; "Avoid repeated or boilerplate text"; "Avoid keyword stuffing"; "Brand your titles concisely"; no length limit but "the title link is truncated in Google Search results as needed, typically to fit the device width." Snippet doc: descriptions must be "truly descriptive"; "meta descriptions comprised of long strings of keywords don't give users a clear idea of the page's content"; "Snippets are primarily created from the page content itself." Every page-1 competitor title for the target queries contains 'Authenticator' and/or 'Autofill' (e.g. 'Authenticator - Chrome Web Store', 'Quickfill – Gmail OTP & 2FA Code Autofill'). ACTION: e.g. <title>AuthPeek – Open-source authenticator extension for Chrome that autofills 2FA codes</title> (brand first, consistent with the manifest name 'AuthPeek – Authenticator & Code Autofill'); keep the description one sentence of what + one of how, ~155 chars, and make the H1 and first paragraph say the same thing in plain words so Google's generated snippet matches.

findings.claim: Structured data: add SoftwareApplication JSON-LD that mirrors visible text; FAQPage markup no longer produces anything in Google (restricted 2023, deprecated May 2026); no schema is required for AI features.
findings.detail: Google SoftwareApplication doc: required properties name and offers.price ("If the app is available without payment, set offers.price to 0"), and "You must include one of the following properties:" aggregateRating or review for the rich result; recommended applicationCategory ("The value must be a supported app type", e.g. SecurityApplication) and operatingSystem; Google does not guarantee a rich result and "Google may take manual action" for violations. Google's structured-data changelog: Sept 14 2023 — FAQ rich results "only shown for well-known, authoritative government and health websites"; May 8 2026 entry — FAQ rich result no longer appears from May 7 2026; June 15 2026 — FAQ documentation removed. AI features doc: "no special schema.org structured data that you need to add"; May 2025 post: "make sure that all the content in your markup is also visible on your web page." ACTIONS: add one SoftwareApplication block with name, description, applicationCategory 'SecurityApplication', operatingSystem 'Chrome', offers {price 0, priceCurrency USD}, softwareVersion '1.1.3', url, installUrl/downloadUrl = Web Store URL, author (Person), sameAs = GitHub repo, license URL — only fields that are visible on the page; omit aggregateRating/review until the Web Store has real ratings (a new extension cannot honestly qualify for the rich result yet); write the FAQ as visible HTML without FAQPage markup; carry datePublished/dateModified on a WebPage object matching the visible date.

findings.claim: Freshness measurably helps on ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini and Perplexity (not on Google AI Overviews); show a real, labeled 'Last updated' date matched by dateModified, and never bump it without content changes.
findings.detail: Ahrefs, July 28 2025 (16.975M cited URLs across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, AI Overviews and organic Google): AI-cited pages were 25.7% fresher by publish date (average 1064 vs 1432 days old); ChatGPT citations 458 days newer than organic results, ChatGPT in-text references 393, Copilot 360, Gemini 298, Perplexity 250; Google AI Overviews 16 days older; last-updated gap 13.1%. Ahrefs notes Mueller "has warned against updating publish dates without any corresponding changes in the page content" and that "Content freshness is one among many factors". Google publication-dates doc: show a visible date labelled e.g. 'Publish' or 'Last updated'; use datePublished and/or dateModified; "Ensure that the date (and optional time and timezone) match between the equivalent user-visible and structured values"; "The dates must describe the publication or update date of the page, not the stories or events described therein." ACTION: add 'Last updated: <date> · v1.1.3' plus a short changelog section tied to real releases.

findings.claim: Sitemap and robots.txt are trivial on GitHub Pages: hand-write both (the docs folder is plain HTML) or enable the whitelisted jekyll-sitemap / jekyll-seo-tag plugins.
findings.detail: GitHub Pages dependency versions page lists jekyll-sitemap 1.4.0, jekyll-seo-tag 2.8.0 and jekyll-feed 0.17.0 as supported; GitHub docs: "You can enable additional plugins by adding the plugin's gem to the plugins setting in your _config.yml file" and "GitHub Pages cannot build sites using unsupported plugins." Google sitemap overview: a sitemap may be unnecessary for sites of "about 500 pages or fewer" that are "comprehensively linked internally", but "in most cases, your site will benefit from having a sitemap." Both files currently return 404 on the AuthPeek site. ACTION: add docs/robots.txt (User-agent: * / Allow: / / Sitemap: https://lazizjanasatov.github.io/Authpeek/sitemap.xml) and docs/sitemap.xml listing / and /privacy.html with <lastmod>; submit the sitemap in Search Console. jekyll-seo-tag would also generate title, description, canonical, OG, Twitter and JSON-LD, but requires converting the pages to Jekyll with front matter.

findings.claim: Crawler access: all four vendors' search crawlers must be allowed to be cited; with no robots.txt they already are, and GitHub's own robots.txt lets OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity bots read the README.
findings.detail: OpenAI: "OAI-SearchBot is used to surface websites in search results in ChatGPT's search features"; "Sites that are opted out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers"; GPTBot is training-only and independent of search; ChatGPT-User fetches on user request and "robots.txt rules may not apply"; ~24 hours for robots.txt changes to apply. Anthropic: Claude-SearchBot "navigates the web to improve search result quality for users"; blocking Claude-User "may reduce your site's visibility for user-directed web search"; bots honor robots.txt; IP list at claude.com/crawling/bots.json. Perplexity: "we recommend allowing PerplexityBot in your site's robots.txt"; Perplexity-User "generally ignores robots.txt rules" and may "include a link to the page in its response"; IP JSON at perplexity.com/perplexitybot.json. Google: Googlebot is the control for Search/AI features; Google-Extended only affects training/grounding elsewhere. GitHub robots.txt: User-agent * may crawl /owner/repo (README) and explicitly lists GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai and PerplexityBot with "Crawl-delay: 1" and the same disallow list (/tree/, /blame/, /raw/, /commits/ etc. blocked). None of the four vendor docs mentions sitemaps, llms.txt or how sources are ranked. ACTION: keep robots.txt permissive (no Disallow, no Google-Extended/GPTBot blocks if you want ChatGPT/Gemini to use the content); keep the README as the canonical factual description since it is reachable by every crawler.

findings.claim: llms.txt is not read by Google or, per their own crawler documentation, by OpenAI, Anthropic or Perplexity; skip it or treat it as a harmless 5-minute extra.
findings.detail: John Mueller (Google) on Bluesky, June 17 2025: "FWIW no AI system currently uses llms.txt" and, of consumer chatbots, "none of them fetch the llms.txt file." Google's AI features doc: "You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, or markup to appear in these features." The OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity crawler pages do not mention llms.txt as an input. The llms.txt proposal itself (Jeremy Howard, published Sept 3 2024, last modified Aug 10 2026) makes no claim that any vendor consumes it; it only notes that labs publish llms.txt for their own docs and that Chrome's Lighthouse audits for one. I could not find any Bing statement either way. Vendor claims of 'no measurable effect' studies were only seen second-hand (low confidence).

findings.claim: Open Graph tags are missing; add the four required properties plus og:description and og:image:alt so shares on Reddit/HN/Twitter/LinkedIn render a card.
findings.detail: ogp.me: "The four required properties for every page are" og:title, og:type, og:image ("An image URL which should represent your object within the graph"), og:url ("The canonical URL of your object that will be used as its permanent ID in the graph"); optional og:description ("A one to two sentence description of your object"), og:site_name, og:image:width/height, and "If the page specifies an og:image it should specify og:image:alt." ACTION: og:type website, og:url = https://lazizjanasatov.github.io/Authpeek/, og:image = the existing auto-fill screenshot/GIF still (1200x630 recommended by platforms, not by the spec), og:image:alt, plus twitter:card summary_large_image; this directly supports the Reddit/HN posts in the off-site findings.

findings.claim: Off-site venues and their rules: Show HN and existing Reddit threads already rank for these queries; AlternativeTo and Product Hunt are free but did not appear among cited domains in any study or live test.
findings.detail: Hacker News Show HN rules: for things people can try; excludes landing pages, sign-up pages, blog posts; make it easy to try without signup; HN guidelines: "Please don't use HN primarily for promotion." and "please use the original title, unless it is misleading or linkbait; don't editorialize." A Show HN for Faktor ('The missing 2FA code autocomplete for Chrome', Jul 3 2024) ranks on Google page 1 for 'how to autofill 2FA codes in Chrome'. Product Hunt FAQ: "you cannot ask people directly to upvote your product"; "We encourage makers to hunt their own products"; "You can launch as often as you have new significant product iterations available"; "It's 100% free to use." AlternativeTo FAQ: submit via 'Suggest new application' after email verification with Platforms, License, Descriptions, Tags; the normal queue holds "several thousand apps"; paid "Priority submissions are usually reviewed within 1-2 business days" (fee does not affect approval); open-source flag and source link supported. Reddit: official policy pages returned HTTP 403 to my fetches; Rule 2 (authentic content, no spam/manipulation) known only via secondary sources; each subreddit sets its own self-promotion rules. ACTIONS (in order): Show HN with GitHub + Web Store links and a candid write-up of the encrypted-sync and autofill design; disclosed replies in r/Bitwarden 'Best 2FA extensions for Google Chrome?' and the Mar 2026 'official authenticator extension' thread; AlternativeTo listing as an alternative to Google Authenticator / Authenticator (authenticator.cc); Product Hunt last.

findings.claim: Avoid: incentivized, affiliated or self-authored reviews/ratings/installs, keyword-stuffed listing copy, paid links, fake date bumps and chasing the Featured badge; each is a Chrome Web Store policy violation or shown not to help.
findings.detail: Chrome Web Store 'Spam and abuse' policy: prohibited manipulation "includes, but is not limited to, inflating product ratings, reviews, or install counts" through "fraudulent or incentivized downloads, reviews and ratings" (2020 Chromium blog/Sophos coverage adds reviews by the developer or affiliates; secondary). Listing guidance: "Repetitive or irrelevant use of keywords" can lead to suspension. Ahrefs: backlinks correlate only 0.218 with AI Overview visibility vs 0.664 for brand mentions. GEO paper: keyword stuffing lowered Position-Adjusted Word Count 19.5→17.8. Mueller/Ahrefs: do not refresh dates without content changes. CWS Aug 20 2026: "we're sunsetting the 'Featured' badge program later this year" and self-nominations are closed.

findings.claim: Side finding on the user's complaint: the redesigned Chrome Web Store shows reviews only on the /reviews sub-page, holds some for moderation, and header ratings lag; publishers and affiliates may not rate their own item.
findings.detail: chromium-extensions Google Group, Oliver Dunk (DevRel, Chrome Extensions): Jan 17 2025 — "the team made a product decision to make that section more concise, and to use the /reviews page to show the actual reviews"; Nov 22 2024 — "I would always wait a couple of days before becoming concerned"; Nov 27 2025 — "The ratings displayed in the header are calculated periodically, and so they can lag behind what you see elsewhere"; Dec 3 2025 — a review email linking to a not-found page is "likely ... either being held for moderation or was deleted". Developer doc 'Manage user feedback': "Each user can only rate an extension once"; "you cannot remove user comments from your listing"; developers may reply. Spam policy bars inflating ratings via incentivized/affiliated reviews, which is consistent with the publisher being unable to rate their own item (exact mechanism not found in primary docs — low confidence on that detail). ACTION: check https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/<extension-id>/reviews rather than the main page; allow a few days; if legitimate reviews are still missing, post the extension ID in the chromium-extensions group thread; do not ask friends/affiliates to rate.

findings.claim: Unconfirmed items: how ChatGPT search selects sources (Bing involvement), Gemini behaviour, and GitHub's share of AI citations.
findings.detail: OpenAI's crawler doc does not say how ChatGPT chooses or ranks sources; its help article on ChatGPT search returned HTTP 403, so the widely reported Bing/third-party-provider statement could not be read first-hand. Gemini was not tested and no Gemini-specific guidance beyond the Ahrefs freshness data (Gemini citations 298 days newer than organic) was found. No study quantifying github.com's citation share for developer-tool queries was found; the only claim (xseek.io) is a vendor page without methodology. The Peec AI 30M-source study was reachable only via a Search Engine Land page that returned 403.

research.summary: Research on what reads as "premium" in authenticator/password-manager extensions (1Password, Bitwarden, Proton Pass, Ente Auth, 2FAS, Authenticator.cc, Raycast), drawn mainly from Google's extension docs, the vendors' own help/blog pages and their open-source UI code. Key implementable patterns: Chrome clamps popups to 25x25–800x600 px (Bitwarden ships 380/480/600 px widths, 600 px max height); codes are set in Inter (Proton, Ente, Bitwarden legacy) or a monospace stack (Bitwarden TOTP field) at ~24 px, grouped "123 456"; countdowns are a 28–36 px ring with the seconds number inside that turns warning/danger at ≤10 s / ≤5–7 s (Proton, Bitwarden) or a 3 px top bar that turns orange at 40% (Ente); every product has tap-to-copy with a toast, type-to-search on open, pin/favourites, hide/reveal codes, light/dark/system themes and a brand-logo per entry fetched through a vendor proxy or a CC0/Apache/CC-BY icon set (Simple Icons, Dashboard Icons, selfh.st, aegis-icons) or Chrome's own _favicon API. Chrome Web Store review pages sit behind a consent wall, so review sentiment comes from the App Store, AMO and Bitwarden's community forum; Bitwarden's current --font-sans value and 2FAS's icon file spec could not be confirmed.

findings.claim: Chrome clamps an action popup to between 25x25 and 800x600 CSS px and auto-sizes it to content; Firefox uses the same 800x600 ceiling and wants the width set on <body>, not :root.
findings.detail: Google's action API reference: "The popup's size must be between 25x25 and 800x600 pixels" and it "will be automatically sized to fit its contents." MDN: Firefox grows the popup "to a size of 800x600 pixels at most if that fits on the user's screen", recalculates size on DOM mutations up to 10x/second, and says "When setting the popup width in CSS, you should set it in the <body> and not in the :root." Implementable: fix body width explicitly (e.g. 380–480 px), cap height at 600 px, scroll the list inside, never rely on the popup growing beyond 800x600; browser zoom eats into the cap so keep layouts under ~750x550 CSS px (third-party extension.js guidance).

findings.claim: Bitwarden's redesigned extension ships three widths — narrow 380 px, default 480 px, wide 600 px — caps height at 600 px, opens its pop-out window at 630 px tall, and adapts layout with height classes.
findings.detail: browser-popup-utils.ts: `PopupWidthOptions = { default: 480, wide: 600, narrow: 380 }`; popout `height: 630`. popup-size.service.ts: `MAX_EXT_HEIGHT = 600`; adds `body-3xs` (<300 px available), `body-xxs` (<400), `body-xs` (<500), `body-sm` (<600) or `body-full` (running in a tab) to the root so CSS can collapse chrome when the browser gives less height. Code comment: old "wide" (480) became "default", old "extraWide" (600) became "wide". The help page still labels them "default width, wide, or extra wide" and adds "Compact mode (beta): Condense the amount of whitespace between elements" and "Show animations ... a slide effect when you change views".

findings.claim: Users punished Bitwarden's December 2024 redesign for being too wide and too sparse — density controls (narrow width, real compact mode) are a premium signal, not a nicety.
findings.detail: Community thread (24–26 Dec 2024): "only options to make it MORE wide and not LESS"; new version is "super huge"; Compact Mode "doesn't seem to really do anything at all"; sidebar version noticeably wider. A separate search surfaced the complaint that the redesign shows "a measly 5 vault items" without scrolling. Bitwarden responded in its blog by adding "classic behavior" toggles (quick copy actions on the list, click-anywhere-to-fill, collapsible Favorites/All items). Implementable: ship a compact row (~48 px) option and keep 6–8 codes visible in a 600 px popup.

findings.claim: Inter is the de-facto UI typeface across the premium set (Proton Pass, Ente Auth, Bitwarden's popup SCSS); Bitwarden sets the TOTP value itself in a monospace stack. Inter is OFL-licensed and has tabular-figure and slashed-zero OpenType features suited to code digits.
findings.detail: Proton Pass extension Popup.scss: `body { font-family: var(--optional-font-family, 'Inter'); }`; Proton _fonts.scss loads Inter 400/500/600/700 and `InterVariable` (`font-weight: 100 900`) with OpenDyslexic and Atkinson Hyperlegible as accessibility alternatives. Ente Auth ships Inter Light/Regular/Medium/SemiBold/Bold. Bitwarden popup variables.scss: `$font-family-sans-serif: Inter, "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;` and `$font-family-monospace: Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Courier New", monospace;`; the TOTP input uses `class="tw-font-mono"`. Inter page: OFL 1.1; `tnum` "Fixed-width numbers are useful for tabular data", `zero` slashed zero, `ss01` alternate digits, `ss02` disambiguation. MDN: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` = OpenType `tnum`, `slashed-zero` = `zero`, Baseline since Jan 2020. Implementable: `font-family: Inter; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums slashed-zero;` on the code so digits don't jitter on roll-over. Bitwarden's new Tailwind theme maps `sans: var(--font-sans)` but the variable's value was not found in tw-theme.css.

findings.claim: Code digits are shown large (24 px normal / 14 px compact in Ente) and grouped with a space: Proton and Ente use groups of three ("123 456"), Bitwarden splits in half.
findings.detail: Ente code_widget.dart: current code `AutoSizeText` `fontSize: isCompactMode ? 14 : 24`; next code grey at 18/12; issuer `titleLarge` (compact: `bodyMedium`); account `bodySmall` 12 px grey. `_getFormattedCode`: 6→"123 456", 7→3-1-3, 8→3-2-3, 9→3-3-3; hidden codes mask every non-space char with `•`. Proton OTPValue.tsx: `if (!code || code.length % 3) return code;` then `chunk(Array.from(code), 3)` joined with a single space. Bitwarden totp-countdown.component.ts: `half = Math.floor(code.length / 2)`, `code.substring(0, half) + " " + code.substring(half)`; placeholder `'*** ***'`. 2FAS tutorial: default style shows larger codes, "The compact style ... presents smaller codes with less spacing between them."

findings.claim: The countdown convention in extensions is a small ring (28–36 px) with the remaining seconds inside, turning warning/danger near expiry; Ente instead uses a thin top bar that turns orange; Authenticator.cc uses a CSS pie.
findings.detail: Bitwarden totp-countdown.component.html: `<svg class="tw-size-7" transform="rotate(-90)" viewBox="0 0 28 28">` with inner circle r=9.5 stroke-width 2 dasharray 60 (progress via `stroke-dashoffset` = `60/period*elapsed`) and outer circle r=11 stroke-width 1 as static track; seconds in a `<span bitTypography="helper" aria-hidden="true">`; `totpLow` when `period - mod <= 7` switches to `tw-stroke-danger-600`/`tw-text-danger`. Proton OTPDonut.tsx: canvas `size = 36`, `thickness = 3`, start angle -π/2, colours from CSS vars `--text-hint` (empty), `--signal-success` (filled), `--signal-warning` when `countDown <= 10`, `--signal-danger` when `<= 5`; number via `::before { content: var(--countdown-value); font-size: rem(12); color: var(--text-weak) }`; wrapper `anime-fade-in pointer-events-none`; dark-theme listener re-reads colours.
